evidence.quote: these FAQs seek to provide additional guidance on the implications of the licensing regime under the Securities and Futures Ordinance (the “Ordinance”) to single family offices and multi-family offices.
three key factors, all of which must be present in order to give rise to a licensing obligation
The issue of whether a multi-family office is required to be licensed under the Ordinance will be primarily determined by the three key factors set out in the response to Q3.
the licensing regime does not hinge on whether an entity is called a family office or whether its clients are families.
will need to be determined by reference to the facts of each case

decisions.reasoning: This purpose and audience statement materially qualifies the scope of the selected control: the guidance covers both single and multi-family offices, with Q5 expressly referring multi-family offices to Q3. It is not an executable condition or an additional Boolean input. After resolving regulated-activity carve-outs, Q3 requires regulated activity, carrying on a business in those services, and carrying on that business in Hong Kong together. Office labels do not establish those conditions, and the business assessment remains fact-dependent. Q5’s qualification “primarily” must be retained; the introductory statement alone does not establish exhaustive application to every arrangement. The requested outcome concerns the licensing trigger, not possession of a licence. Missing authority remains unverified.
